verdict.rationale: GrowthBook documents some portability of its own: OpenFeature support so switching away only changes the provider bootstrap, a REST API that can pull experiment results into your own reporting, exportable audit logs, and a warehouse-native design where metric data stays in your warehouse. It is also open source and self-hostable on its own MongoDB. However, the evidence documents no bulk 'export all data' feature or named open export format. missing for 10: documented full-account data export (flags, experiments, metrics, settings), specified open export formats, a migration/offboarding guide, independent hands-on corroboration of a complete export.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can export all of my data in open formats and leave

citations.quote: Switching from or to GrowthBook only requires changing the provider bootstrap, not a single flag call.
Get results for an experiment (`GET /v1/experiments/{id}/results`) to pull the latest analysis into your own reporting.
GrowthBook offers a full REST API for interacting with the application.
Warehouse Native. Query 11 data sources including BigQuery, Snowflake, and Databricks.
